The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Given $g(t)={\int }_{-3}^{t}f(x)\,\text{d}x,$ determine the value of $g(3).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Evaluating $g(t)$ at $t=3,$ we get the following definite integral:

$$
g(3)={\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

This integral gives the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14010573/assets/b14fbfe336923b44e4e4f3660bef7c6be97ada82ea07c4523a3f25f2905f4fd6.png)

Note that the graph above consists of $2$ parts:

- $x\in [-3,0],$ for which the region between the curve and the $x$-axis is a triangle. This corresponds to the area ${A}_{1}.$

- $x\in [0,3],$  for which the region between the curve and the $x$-axis is a square.  This corresponds to the area ${A}_{2}.$

Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
g(3)={\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}
$$

Now, let's compute these integrals:

- To find the first integral where $x\in [-3,0],$ we compute the area ${A}_{1}$ of the triangle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- To find the second integral where $x\in [0,3],$ we compute the area ${A}_{2}$ of the triangle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={3}^{2} \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}g(3) & ={\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=\frac{9}{2}+9=\frac{27}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
